$comment: BMW S54B32 as fitted to the E46 M3 and M3 CSL (launch swap). Researched 2026-09-27. Primary sources: BMW NA technical training ST041 (E46 M3), ST055 (MS S54), ST505 (M engines) and ST601 (Z4 M) on archive.org; BMW AG, BMW GB and BMW NA press kits; ETK via bmwfans.info. Dry weight is derived from a BMW statement and outline dimensions are a geometric estimate (see methods). Z3 M and Z4 M ratings are noted but not modelled.

sources.title: BMW of North America Technical Training ST041, module "M Engines - S54B32" (E46 M3, M roadster, M coupe; 2001 MY on), pp. 3-26 (PDF on archive.org, file "2 M3 DriveLine")
sources.note: p. 26: "The S54 uses Bosch (4 hole plate) fuel injectors. The ECM controls the fuel injectors to regulate the air/fuel mixture."; ST041 Engine Electronics: "The Fuel Injectors will be opened by the ECM to inject pressurized fuel into the intake ports."

fuelInjection.note: Sequential port injection with six individual throttle bodies (BMW NA 2003 story: "All six throttles operate from a single shaft, each in its own throttle body right at the intake ports").

sources.title: BMW Media Information 3/2007 "The new V8 Power Unit for the BMW M3."
sources.note: "BMW’s new V8, weighing a mere 202 kg or 445 lb, is a genuine lightweight, saving some 15 kg or 33 lb versus the six-cylinder power unit in the previous model."

dryWeight.method: BMW Media Information 3/2007 gives the V8 that replaced it at 202 kg and says it saves "some 15 kg" against the six-cylinder of the previous M3 (the S54): 202 + 15 = about 217 kg. BMW does not say what the figure includes, and "some" makes it approximate. Forum posts (not opened) cite 217 kg from an M3 brochure; mywikimotors' 149 kg is too low for an engine whose bare iron block alone weighs about 48 kg (ST041).

length.method: No outline dimensions exist in any BMW source found (ST041, ST505/ST609, ST055, press kits, US brochures) or in the aggregators. Geometric estimate for the bare engine with its intake and exhaust manifolds, upright, from BMW's own internal dimensions: bore spacing 91 mm, 91 mm stroke, 139 mm rods (ST041) and a 32.3 mm piston compression height (mywikimotors) give a deck height of about 217 mm above the crank centre. Length: 6 x 91 mm of cylinder row plus block end walls (about 600 mm), the timing case, VANOS unit and vibration damper at the front (about 150 mm) and the crank flange at the rear; about 780 mm, +/-60 mm.

height.method: No outline dimensions exist in any BMW source found (ST041, ST505/ST609, ST055, press kits, US brochures) or in the aggregators. Geometric estimate for the bare engine with its intake and exhaust manifolds, upright, from BMW's own internal dimensions: bore spacing 91 mm, 91 mm stroke, 139 mm rods (ST041) and a 32.3 mm piston compression height (mywikimotors) give a deck height of about 217 mm above the crank centre. Height: about 217 mm deck height plus about 190 mm of head and cam cover above the deck and about 240 mm of crank throw clearance and oil pan below the crank centre; about 650 mm upright, +/-60 mm. In the E46 the engine is installed inclined.

bellhousing.note: The S54 bolts to the same BMW six-cylinder gearbox families as the M54: the Z3 M uses the ZF S5D 320Z with the same part number as the E46 330Ci M54 (23 00 7 503 993), and the Z4 M the ZF GS6-37BZ also used behind the 330Ci M54 from 03/2003. Crank flange: 8 x M12x1.5x50 flywheel bolts. One ETK mirror; no BMW text names the pattern. The E46 M3 dual-mass flywheel is 11.4 kg (ETK).

sources.title: BMW of North America Technical Training ST041, module "M Engines - S54B32" (E46 M3, M roadster, M coupe; 2001 MY on), pp. 3-26 (PDF on archive.org, file "2 M3 DriveLine")
sources.note: p. 10, Oil Pump: "The oil pump has two separate chambers, the scavenge chamber (1) draws oil from the pickup at the front of the oil pan. The oil is transferred from the pump through a small pipe to the main sump at the rear of the oil pan (2)." Oil circuit legend p. 9: "1. Oil Pump Intake (rear of pan) ... 1a. Oil Pump Intake (front of Pan)".

sump.note: E46 M3 layout: the deep main sump is at the rear of the pan with a scavenge pickup at the front (BMW calls it "semi-dry-sump": "a “semi-dry-sump” system helps ensure adequate lubrication under the high cornering, acceleration and braking loads", BMW NA 2003 story). The ST041 module covers the E46 M3 and the Z3 M roadster/coupe; whether the Z3 M or Z4 M pans differ is not stated there.

sources.title: mywikimotors.com: BMW E46 M3 engine | S54 specs (AGGREGATOR)
sources.note: "The maximum boost VT1 – 6 psi (0.4 bar) you do not even need forged pistons. It will easily provide 470 horsepower."

value.note: Both pages trace to ESS Tuning's own description of its VT1-475 kit.

reportedLimits.context: ESS VT1-475 centrifugal supercharger kit rating (non-intercooled): 470 hp SAE (475 DIN) and 330 lb-ft at 6.5 psi on the stock internals. A kit rating from its maker, not a tested failure limit; no fuel, rpm or duration context. The known weak point is the connecting-rod bearings (BMW campaigns 11 02 03 and 11 04 04 replaced them on cars built up to 2003-05-22, per EuroConnex).
